hmmt-feb-2001-gen2-04.prompt: Some students are taking a math contest, in which each student takes one of four tests. One third of the students take one test, one fourth take another test, one fifth take the next test, and $26$ students take the last test. How many students are taking the contest in total?

hmmt-feb-2001-gen2-05.prompt: What is the area of a square inscribed in a semicircle of radius $1$, with one of its sides flush with the diameter of the semicircle?

hmmt-feb-2001-gen2-06.prompt: You take a wrong turn on the way to MIT and end up in Transylvania, where $99\%$ of the inhabitants are vampires and the rest are regular humans. For obvious reasons, you want to be able to figure out who's who. On average, nine-tenths of the vampires are correctly identified as vampires and nine-tenths of humans are correctly identified as humans. What is the probability that someone identified as a human is actually a human?

hmmt-feb-2001-gen2-07.prompt: A real number $x$ is randomly chosen in the interval $\left[-15\frac12,\,15\frac12\right]$. Find the probability that the closest integer to $x$ is odd.
hmmt-feb-2001-gen2-07.reviewNote: Official answer is 15/31. The odd integers from -15 to 15 number 16 (the even ones number 15), so the probability is 16/31. Stored 16/31.

hmmt-feb-2001-gen2-09.prompt: Two circles are concentric. The area of the ring between them is $A$. In terms of $A$, find the length of the longest chord contained entirely within the ring.
